It’s Mental Health Awareness Week, and one thing we don’t think gets spoken about enough is the impact financial stress can have on people’s mental health.

As accountants, we often see the side people don’t publicly talk about:

* the anxiety before opening HMRC letters,
* sleepless nights over cash flow,
* people putting off asking for help,
* business owners carrying pressure silently,
* and individuals avoiding their finances altogether because it feels overwhelming.

Financial stress can affect relationships, confidence, sleep, productivity, and overall wellbeing far more than many people realise.

Research consistently shows a strong link between money worries and mental health challenges, with debt and financial uncertainty being among the leading causes of stress and anxiety in the UK.

One thing we’ve learned working with clients is that avoiding the issue nearly always makes the stress worse. Most financial situations become far more manageable once there’s a plan, clarity, and open communication.

Whether it’s tax, debt, cash flow, or simply not knowing where you stand financially - asking for help early is never something to feel uncomfortable about.

Sometimes people don’t need judgement.
They just need clarity and support.

GLP-1 medications can affect more than appetite.

One of the most interesting (and sometimes surprising) areas we’re seeing in clinical care is mood.

Some patients report:

* improved mental clarity
* less “food noise”
* reduced impulsive eating
* improved confidence and energy

Others may notice:

* increased anxiety
* emotional blunting
* irritability
* changes in motivation or mood

Why?

The answer is likely complex.

GLP-1 medications interact with pathways involved in:

* reward
* dopamine signaling
* inflammation
* blood sugar regulation
* sleep
* stress physiology
* and the gut-brain connection

For many people, the effects are positive.
For others, adjustments in dosing, nutrition, sleep, hydration, or medication strategy may be needed.

As obesity medicine evolves, we are continuing to learn just how interconnected metabolic and emotional health can be.

Wat eerst als mission impossible leek,
heb ik uiteindelijk toch possible gemaakt…

want ik heb dus blijkbaar een boek geschreven. 🤣

Geen idee hoe dit is gebeurd.
Echt niet.

Ik zocht ooit een speelse, luchtige autobiografie
over bewustwording, spiritualiteit en zelfontwikkeling.

Geschreven vanuit een beetje:
“fuck alles” energie.

Je weet wel:
rebels,
eigengereid,
speels,
luchtig,
en niet zo verschrikkelijk zwaar allemaal. 😵‍💫

Kon ik niet vinden.

Dus dacht ik:

Fuck it, dan schrijf ik ‘m zelf wel ff.

Nooit verwacht dat ik dat ook écht zou doen.

En voor ik het wist:

252 pagina’s.
13 thema’s.
En blijkbaar zelfs een inleiding, dankwoord, nawoord en toegift. 😆

Over mijn shit.
Mijn hoofd.
Mijn struggles.
Mijn chaos.
Mijn gevecht met het leven.

Geen standaard zelfhulpboek.
Geen “10 stappen naar geluk”.
Geen saaie, zware of zweverige bullshit.

Maar gewoon:

👉 rauw
👉 eerlijk
👉 kwetsbaar
👉 ongefilterd
👉 met een flinke dosis zelfspot
👉 en diepgang zonder zwaar of zweverig gedoe

Waarom je dit boek zou willen lezen?

Omdat je jezelf gaat herkennen.
Keihard.

In je hoofd.
In je twijfels.
In dat moment dat je denkt:

“Wat ben ik in godsnaam aan het doen?”

Omdat je gaat zien
dat je niet de enige bent.

Met overdenken.
Jezelf saboteren.
Zoeken naar richting.
Jezelf niet goed genoeg voelen.
En het leven soms gewoon niet snappen.

Omdat dit boek eigenlijk één grote spiegel is.

En nee…
niet zo’n gezellige:
“Ik zie er goed uit vandaag”-spiegel.

Maar meer zo’n:
“Ah kut… dit ben ik dus ook.” spiegel. 😆

En nee…

Dit boek gaat je ook niet fixen.

Maar het kan wel iets losmaken.

Een inzicht.
Een shift.
Of gewoon dat ene moment dat je denkt:

“Ah… dus zo zit het.”

Want het is niet alleen maar lachen.

Het is ook:
jezelf tegenkomen.

En ja…
dat is soms gewoon kut. 😏

Dus bij deze…

Het boek komt eraan. 🤪

Postpartum psychosis is a medical emergency that can include:
• Hallucinations or delusions
• Confusion or paranoia
• Rapid mood swings
• Loss of touch with reality
If you or someone you know is experiencing signs of psychosis including hearing or seeing things that are not there, feeling like they are “out of body” and doing things that seem abnormal/unsafe, or are talking about things that do not seem to make sense or are real, seek emergency professional support immediately including but not limited to the nearest emergency room. 
While it seems scary, this is a severe hormonal imbalance heightened by lack of sleep and other factors that needs professional support and monitoring. 
Mental Health Awareness Month is about breaking stigma — especially around the parts of postpartum that people are often too afraid to talk about.
Parents deserve to know:
🤍 You are not alone
🤍 You are not “crazy” or broken
🤍 Help and treatment exist
🤍 Speaking up is a sign of strength, not failure
If you or someone you love is struggling postpartum, reaching out for support can be lifesaving. Contact our doula team for support if you need help finding resources. 
We are here for you.

Mental health can still be one of the loneliest things to carry, even in a room full of people. That’s why spaces like @archstreetcenter matter so much.

Community members gathered for Arch Street’s annual Fishbowl Fundraiser, this year transformed into a luau-themed evening filled with music, laughter, raffles, and conversations that reminded people they are not alone. 

But underneath the tropical shirts and decorations was a room full of people showing up for adults living with serious mental illness and reminding them they deserve connection, stability, dignity, and community without judgment.

For more than four decades, Arch Street has quietly become a lifeline for many in Lancaster County. While conversations around mental health have become more visible in recent years, there are still countless individuals who experience isolation, stigma, and the feeling of being forgotten. 

Arch Street continues to meet people where they are, offering not just programs and services, but a place where members can simply exist without needing to explain themselves first.

The fundraiser was centered around belonging with the fundraising total reaching nearly $92,000!

One of the most emotional parts of the evening was knowing this year’s Fishbowl was also the final one for my dear friend, Susanne Hershey, Development Director. Anyone who has spent time in Lancaster’s nonprofit community knows Susanne’s impact reaches far beyond fundraising. She has spent years building relationships, advocating for organizations that serve vulnerable communities, and helping people feel welcomed the moment they walk into a room. She is someone who pours herself fully into the work and into the people around her.

Her work has helped strengthen not only Arch Street Center, but the broader culture of compassion surrounding #mentalhealth in Lancaster County.

Mental health recovery doesn’t happen in isolation. It happens through community, through organizations willing to remind people they still matter during the hardest seasons of their lives.

That is what Arch Street Center, continues to do. And Lancaster showed up to make sure that work continues too.

You don’t have to be perfect to make progress.

More sets don’t automatically mean more results.

Discipline isn’t about making your life smaller.
It’s about knowing what you want badly enough to make the right choices most of the time.

Years of training taught me more than how to build a physique.

Discipline will change your life forever.

Every goal, every dream, every level of growth requires sacrifice, focus, and consistency. The problem is that distractions are everywhere — social media, negativity, excuses, gossip, comfort, and temporary pleasures that pull people away from their purpose.

Discipline is waking up when you don’t feel like it.

Discipline is protecting your mind, your habits, your health, and your time.

Most people want results, but few are willing to stay committed when things become uncomfortable. That’s where separation happens.

The people who grow are not always the most talented. They are often the ones who learn to stay disciplined while others stay distracted.

Choose the workout.
Choose the study session.
Choose the healing.
Choose the growth.
Choose the long-term vision over short-term pleasure.

Because every disciplined choice you make today is building the life you will live tomorrow.

Lo dice anche l'intelligenza artificiale. Ecco cosa pensa Gemini Ai dello step fatto a scalino Vs. tondo? La risposta dopo aver analizzato il video movimento del piede a confronto:

Ecco la sintesi tecnica del confronto:
1. Massimizzazione dello Stretch (ROM)

  Angolo: L'escursione verso il basso è limitata dal punto di contatto netto; oltre una certa inclinazione, il piede perde aderenza meccanica sullo spigolo, interrompendo l'allungamento.

  Tondo (con Griptape): La superficie curva accoglie il tallone durante la discesa e il nastro antiscivolo mantiene il piede ancorato anche ad angolazioni estreme. Ciò permette un allungamento del polpaccio molto più profondo, fondamentale per innescare l'ipertrofia da stiramento.

2. Biomeccanica e Resistenza Variabile

  Angolo: Il fulcro è fisso e la leva costante. La tensione rimane lineare per tutta la durata della ripetizione.

  Tondo: Il fulcro è mobile. Mentre sali verso la massima contrazione, il punto di contatto rotola leggermente in avanti, modificando il braccio di leva. Questo rende la chiusura del movimento meccanicamente più intensa e stimolante.

3. Gestione del Dolore e Carico Massimale

  Angolo: Il peso è concentrato su una linea sottile. Il dolore da pressione sotto i metatarsi spesso diventa il fattore limitante che impedisce di usare carichi pesanti o di raggiungere il vero cedimento del polpaccio.

  Tondo: La superficie curva distribuisce la pressione su un'area più ampia della pianta del piede. Riducendo il fastidio localizzato, permette di caricare molto di più e di concentrare lo sforzo esclusivamente sul muscolo bersaglio.

In sintesi: Il tubo con griptape risulta superiore per l'ipertrofia poiché garantisce uno stretch più profondo e un comfort pressorio maggiore, consentendo di gestire carichi elevati senza che il dolore plantare o la perdita di aderenza condizionino la serie.
